samples.summary: New CLI hard-requires the backend to echo `state`, breaking `wafflebase login` against every already-deployed older backend (self-hosted installs)
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:280 refuses any callback whose `state` does not match the nonce, and `packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:135` is the only producer of that param. A CLI released from this branch talking to any backend built before this change receives `?code=…` with no `state`, so EVERY genuine login is refused and fails after the timeout. Self-hosting docs (packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:42, packages/backend/README.md:184) state no minimum server version, and the CLI's npm package can be upgraded independently of the server. Mitigation exists (REFUSAL.noState message), but there is no version negotiation or opt-out; consider gating on whether the server advertises support, or documenting a minimum server version alongside the CLI release.

samples.summary: `--format csv` formula neutralization silently diverges CSV from JSON for existing consumers
samples.evidence: scripts/agent/charters/round-trip.md:19 instructs the hunter that "the same data under `--format json` and `--format csv` agrees". After packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:61 passes `neutralizeFormulas: true`, any value starting with `=`,`+`,`-`,`@`,tab,CR gains a `'` prefix in CSV but not JSON, so that invariant no longer holds and the charter will manufacture false findings. The same divergence hits any user pipeline that feeds `sheets cells get --format csv` back through `sheets import` — only `sheets export --file-format csv` was exempted (packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:52).
searchedFor: grep 'format csv' in packages/cli/skills and docs

samples.summary: New comments assert `bin.ts` has no top-level handler; it does (`runCli`), so the stated contract is wrong
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/schema.ts:34-36 ("`bin.ts` has no top-level handler") and packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:119 both describe a contract contradicted by packages/cli/src/cli.ts:75-91, where `runCli` wraps `parseAsync` in try/catch and calls `outputError` for anything unhandled; packages/cli/src/bin.ts:6 only calls `runCli()`. Future callers reading these comments will duplicate handling or mis-reason about escape paths.

samples.summary: `cells batch` dry-run branch moved outside the command's try/catch, changing which handler envelopes a `getConfig` failure
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:147-155 now calls `getConfig(opts)`/`printDryRun` outside any local try. `getConfig` -> `resolveConfig` (packages/cli/src/commands/root.ts:29) can throw for missing server/workspace; previously that produced the command's own `outputError` envelope, now it rejects the action promise and relies on the last-resort catch in packages/cli/src/cli.ts:90. Any embedder or test that drives `program.parseAsync` directly (as packages/cli/test/cells.test.ts does) gets a rejection instead of the envelope.

samples.summary: `ctx list` exit code changed 0 -> 1 when logged out; no consumer found, but scripts using it as a liveness check would now fail
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:76 throws NotLoggedInError (exit 1) where the old code printed prose and returned 0. I searched the repo for consumers and found none outside tests/docs (docs/design/cli.md:1145 documents the new behaviour), so this is a behaviour change with no in-repo breakage — but external wrappers/CI shell scripts using `wafflebase ctx list` as a soft probe would now abort under `set -e`.
searchedFor: grep in scripts/agent for status/ctx invocations

finding.summary: New CLI hard-requires the backend to echo `state`, breaking `wafflebase login` against every already-deployed older backend (self-hosted installs)
finding.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:280 refuses any callback whose `state` does not match the nonce, and `packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:135` is the only producer of that param. A CLI released from this branch talking to any backend built before this change receives `?code=…` with no `state`, so EVERY genuine login is refused and fails after the timeout. Self-hosting docs (packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:42, packages/backend/README.md:184) state no minimum server version, and the CLI's npm package can be upgraded independently of the server. Mitigation exists (REFUSAL.noState message), but there is no version negotiation or opt-out; consider gating on whether the server advertises support, or documenting a minimum server version alongside the CLI release.

verdict.reason: The described code exists (login.ts:279-288 refuses non-matching `state`; auth.controller.ts:131-135 is the sole producer), but it is not a blast-radius defect. A repo-wide grep for the changed contract (`startCallbackServer`, `nonceMatches`, `mode=cli`, `/callback?code`) shows every in-repo consumer is consistent: github-auth.guard.ts:36-40 stores the nonce, cli-auth.store.ts:30-60 round-trips it, auth.controller.ts:131-135 echoes it, and the CLI tests (test/login.test.ts:46, test/login-command.test.ts:143) drive the new form. The only "broken caller" is a previously released backend binary that is not code in this repository, so there is no file:line here that needs to change — this is release/deployment-skew policy, i.e. design-fit, not an unupdated caller or a bypassed guard. Moreover the finding's own remedy is already present: docs/design/cli.md:206-208 explicitly documents the minimum-server-version coupling ("a CLI at this version or later needs a backend at this version or later"), docs/design/rest-api.md:347 documents the `&state=<nonce>` redirect, and login.ts:190-194 + 246 print an immediate, actionable diagnostic naming an out-of-date server rather than a silent hang. The finding's doc citations are also wrong: self-hosting.md:42 is the GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL env line and backend/README.md:184 is an API-table row; neither mentions the CLI or version policy.
